messages:
alex: seeing a sharp p95 jump ~10:35 UTC, affected a subset of hosts in us-west-2. throughput also dipped 20%.
maya: I see the grafana spike, but traces are sparse for the time window. most spans missing on the noisy hosts.
priya: noisy neighbor suspect — one host had a bunch of long-running retrains. any kernel-selection churn around that time?
jordan: we rolled kernel heuristics at 10:20 (small rollout). it changed the kernel selector to prefer fast-int8 for short seqs. could that misfire on batched sequences?
alex: possible. profiling shows jittery tail latencies on kernels with small-reqs+large-batches. attaching a quick perf snippet:
alex: ```
# perf top output (sample)
samples  %  symbol
1200    35  runtime::kernel_dispatch
400     12  attention::fused_kernel
... 
``` 
maya: kv-cache metrics look weird too — eviction rate spikes at the same hosts. eviction burst could magnify cold-cache misses and IO.
priya: dashboard mismatch: token-level latency series is flat but p95 jumps — I think token-level emit got sampled out during the incident window.
jordan: confirmed: trace-sampler change was pushed with reduced sampling to cut cardinality last week. looks like the relabel rule dropped spans with tag host=priority-*. that would remove all traces from dedicated infra hosts.
infra-bot: deploy-bot reports: rollout 2026-11-07T10:20:12Z kernel-heuristics v2 -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% (completed)
deploy-bot: note: trace-sampler config change deployed 2026-11-02T03:12:45Z by ops-automation.
alex: ops, can we temporarily bump trace sampling on the impacted host group? we need full spans for root cause.
priya: doing that now — enabling full traces for us-west-2-group-2 for 30m. also reenabled token-level metrics scrape for those nodes.
maya: after enabling, traces started coming back at ~10:42 and we can see kernel_dispatch queueing on host-32.
jordan: root cause hypothesis: kernel selector + aggressive batching increase -> runtime chose int8 fused kernel that has bad latency characteristics for low-seq high-batch workloads on certain GPU drivers -> combined with KV evictions (caused by noisy retrain jobs) -> tail p95 blows up.
alex: agreed. short-term mitigations: 1) rollback kernel-heuristics to previous version 2) tighten batch max tokens for short-seq routes 3) limit retrain jobs on inference clusters.
priya: rollback kicked at 10:55, p95 trending down. throughput normalizing by 11:05. kv-eviction still elevated but separate follow-up.
maya: observability follow-ups: revert the aggressive trace-sampler relabel, add alert for "trace density drop" so we don't blind ourselves next time, and add a dashboard tile showing spans-per-minute per host.
jordan: will create PRs for kernel-heuristics revert + safer rollout gating (canary perf thresholds), and a change to batch heuristics to prefer smaller batches when seq_len distribution skew detected.
alex: logging note — previously we had log sampling rules that dropped debug-level kernel dispatch logs. enabled debug for 10m on the impacted hosts to capture one more incident trace.
priya: adding postmortem and owners: alex (runtime), jordan (kernel selector), maya (observability), priya (infra ops). scheduled follow-up tomorrow 15:00 UTC.
alex: thanks all. main action items in the thread:
- revert kernel-heuristics rollout (done)
- revert trace-sampler relabel (in progress)
- add trace density alert (todo)
- schedule kernel perf regression test for the fused int8 path (todo)
- limit background retrain IO on inference hosts (ops)
:thumbsup:
